summary.headline: CMR Green FY26 revenue rose 29.5% to ₹8,640 crore and EBITDA 50.4% to ₹449.4 crore; ₹200 crore capex for two new plants underway.
summary.overview: This was the 21st AGM, held by video conference on 29 September 2026, and the first since listing; the Chairman was absent and Akshay Agarwal chaired. Management reported FY26 sales volume up about 24% to 409,000 MT, with revenue of ₹8,640 crore, EBITDA of ₹449.4 crore (margin about 5.2% vs 4.5%) and PAT of ₹228.4 crore (up 47.3%). On the West Asia war, management said scrap supply disruption lifted prices and market share, but margins were mainly driven by operational efficiency since the company is hedged. Capacity plans include two new plants (Shoolagiri and Bawal) and brownfield expansion at four existing plants, taking capacity to 6-7 lakh tonnes by end-2026.

financial_highlights.metric: Per-tonne margin (Q1 post West Asia war)

segments.name: Aluminium recycling
segments.commentary: Primary focus on aluminium scrap recycling into alloys; aluminium volumes rose about 27% in FY26. Company is moving into billets, wrought alloys and green aluminium products.

segments.name: Non-aluminium / other metals
segments.commentary: Zinc alloys and other recycled metal products; non-aluminium sales rose about 18% in FY26. Evaluating copper, lead and lithium-ion battery recycling.

guidance_outlook: Two new plants this year, at Shoolagiri and Bawal, to serve EV-linked aluminium demand; ₹200 crore capex committed, about ₹53 crore spent in Q1.
Brownfield expansions at four existing plants; overall capacity expected to reach 6-7 lakh tonnes by end of calendar 2026.
Management expects an industry CAGR of about 11-13% in the years ahead and aims to grow market share.
Focus on consistent profitability through hedging rather than windfall gains from price spikes.
capex_capacity: Two new plants in 2026: Shoolagiri and Bawal; ₹200 crore capex committed, about ₹53 crore spent in Q1.
Brownfield expansion across four existing plants, taking total capacity to 6-7 lakh tonnes by end-2026 (from 615,000 TPA at 31 March 2026).
Installed solar capacity about 9.55 MW across facilities.
Carbon credits: about 50,000-60,000 tCO2 savings generated annually; cumulative over 270,000 carbon credits.
demand_pricing: Management cited demand drivers: low per-capita aluminium consumption in India, EV, solar panels, packaging and auto.
West Asia conflict disrupted scrap routing via Suez Canal and Strait of Hormuz ports, causing a sharp shortage and steep price increases.
Company says it gained market share during the disruption by servicing customers that competitors could not.
Margin rose to about ₹12.5 per unit in Q1 after the war from about ₹11.5 last year, attributed to efficiency and scale, with hedging limiting windfall gains.

qa_highlights.question: Shareholder Parmod Jain asked for current scrap processing and recycling capacity and expansion plans from IPO proceeds over the next 2-3 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two new plants (Shoolagiri and Bawal) are being built this year with ₹200 crore capex, plus brownfield expansion at four plants, reaching 6-7 lakh tonnes by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Shareholder Rishabh Jain asked about the impact of the West Asia war on aluminium markets and operations.
qa_highlights.answer: Scrap shortages drove prices sharply higher; the company gained share, and per-unit margin rose to about ₹12.5 from ₹11.5, mainly from efficiency since it is hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Shareholder Rishabh Jain asked about steps to reduce carbon footprint.
qa_highlights.answer: Company earns about 50,000-60,000 tCO2 saving credits a year (over 270,000 cumulative) and is cutting Scope 2 and 3 emissions through solar, CNG, electric trucks and EVs for internal fleets.

qa_highlights.question: Shareholder Manjit Singh asked about post-listing growth plans and requested future AGMs be held earlier, in August.
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the two new plants and brownfield expansions, a 11-13% industry CAGR outlook, and market share gains; no response recorded on the AGM timing request.

risks_watch: Scrap supply and pricing volatility from West Asia shipping disruption via Suez Canal and Strait of Hormuz.
Execution risk on Shoolagiri and Bawal plants and four brownfield expansions; track capex spend beyond ₹53 crore and commissioning dates.
Margin sustainability: company says it hedges, so margin gains depend on operating efficiency.
Share price trading below IPO issue price, as raised by a retail shareholder.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and FY26 results, with a focus on execution. Cautious on pricing gains, which management attributed to operations rather than windfall, and on hedging. Answers to shareholder questions were general and gave few figures on the West Asia impact.
key_quotes: But yes, it is now quoting below the issue price, but I am here for the long term.
